description:
lib/defk/divergences.ex is an all-no-op stub: `list/0` and `registry/0` return %{}, `has_divergences?/0` is false, `match?/3` is false, `explain/1` is "", `generate_page!/1` returns :ok without writing anything. Nothing calls it. It was added in the defk-63k scaffolding commit (eeb6230) as a placeholder for the registry that ticket specifies: "Defk.Divergences registry: matcher, explanation, ticket per entry; the checker skips matching cases; it generates the divergence page; done for the verdict requires it empty."

Decide and do one of:
(a) implement it as specified: entries are %{match: (mod, fun, args -> boolean), explanation: String.t, ticket: "defk-xxx"}; Defk.Test.assert_agrees skips a case that matches an entry and reports it as a known divergence; `mix run -e 'Defk.Divergences.generate_page!()'` writes docs/divergences.md; a test asserts the page is up to date; the verdict (defk-sgw.5) requires the registry empty.
(b) delete the module, since the current policy is "each divergence is a bug to remove or turn into a limit" (CONTEXT.md) and limits are documented in docs/language.md, not a registry.

Recommendation: (a) only if the agreement properties (sibling ticket) surface divergences that cannot be fixed before the verdict; otherwise (b). Either way the dead stub should not stay.

Done when: the module is either implemented with a test and wired into assert_agrees, or removed, and README/CONTEXT.md reflect the choice.
title: Implement the Defk.Divergences registry per defk-63k, or delete the stub
